little_st_james.name: Little St. James Island
little_st_james.description: Private island owned by Jeffrey Epstein from 1998 until his death. The island featured a main compound, guest houses, and became central to trafficking allegations.
little_st_james.significance: Central location in trafficking allegations. Multiple victims reported being taken to the island.

great_st_james.name: Great St. James Island
great_st_james.description: Larger island adjacent to Little St. James, purchased by Epstein in 2016.

palm_beach.name: Palm Beach Residence
palm_beach.location: 358 El Brillo Way, Palm Beach, Florida
palm_beach.description: Epstein's Florida mansion where many of the initial allegations originated. This was a key location in the 2005 police investigation.
palm_beach.significance: Site of initial 2005 investigation. Multiple victims recruited from the area.

new_york.name: Manhattan Townhouse
new_york.description: Epstein's massive Manhattan townhouse, one of the largest private residences in New York City. Originally owned by Leslie Wexner.
new_york.significance: Major location for meetings with high-profile individuals. Site of alleged abuse.

paris.name: Paris Apartment
paris.description: Luxury apartment in one of Paris's most exclusive neighborhoods.

new_mexico.name: Zorro Ranch
new_mexico.description: Sprawling ranch in New Mexico where Epstein allegedly planned to seed the human race with his DNA.
new_mexico.significance: Location of alleged abuse. Epstein spoke of creating a 'baby ranch' here.

mar_a_lago.name: Mar-a-Lago Club
mar_a_lago.description: Exclusive resort where Virginia Giuffre was recruited while working as a spa attendant.
mar_a_lago.significance: Location where Ghislaine Maxwell recruited Virginia Giuffre in 1998.

manhattan_jail.name: Metropolitan Correctional Center
manhattan_jail.description: Federal detention facility where Epstein was held and died in 2019.
manhattan_jail.significance: Site of Epstein's death on August 10, 2019.
